$schema-notes.about: Single source of truth for adamnolle.com. Everything on the site is rendered from this file at build time — edit here, run npm run build, done.
$schema-notes.prose links: profile.intro accepts [label](https://example.com). No other markup is allowed anywhere; all values are escaped.
$schema-notes.projects: source is required, site is optional. A project with both shows VISIT and SOURCE; one with only source shows SOURCE. status LIVE draws a filled marker, anything else an outline.
$schema-notes.hero.windowLabel: Text in the hero terminal title bar. Leave empty to hide it.
$schema-notes.site.tabTitle: Browser tab text. site.title is the longer form used for link previews.
$schema-notes.history[].entries[]: current: true tints the role green and fills the timeline marker. marker: true fills it without the tint.
$schema-notes.header tooltips: Icon links show tooltip on hover and label to screen readers. Omit tooltip and it falls back to label.
$schema-notes.site.ogImage: The link-preview card, 1200x630. Rebuild it with npm run assets:og after changing hero.asciiWords or hero.lines.
$schema-notes.header.social[].icon: github, linkedin, youtube, www-globe (the spinning Web World Wide globe baked by npm run assets:globe), or nolle-studios (the four-square Nolle Studios mark).
$schema-notes.history[].entries[].projects: Optional. Projects done within a role, shown as sub-sections: name, what (one line), tags, bullets, and an optional href. projectsLabel heads the list.

projects.name: FileID
projects.description: Point it at a folder and it sorts everything inside, offline. Tags by content, clusters faces into people you name once, groups duplicates, and answers questions about the library with citations. Nothing leaves your machine.

projects.name: Document Finder
projects.description: Searches eight open-access research sources at once, pulls the text out of what it finds, and serves chunked, cited results straight to AI tools over MCP.

projects.name: Media Shuttle
projects.description: Copies photos and videos off camera cards, checks every copy with SHA-256, and will not let you erase the card until every file has a verified copy.

projects.name: Cube Solver
projects.description: Solves 2×2 up to 11×11 puzzle cubes from the sticker colors alone. Scramble it or turn faces yourself, then watch it solve; every answer has to replay back to solved before it counts.

projects.name: Anchor
projects.description: Paused should mean paused. Holds a video you paused until you press play, so ads ending, streams reconnecting and scripted restarts cannot resume it, while next episodes and autoplay keep working.

projects.name: Watched Blocked
projects.description: Hides YouTube videos you've already watched from the home page, sidebar, search and playlists, while channel pages, Subscriptions and History still show everything.

projects.name: Guitar Tutor
projects.description: Fretboard, chord library, ear trainer, metronome. Every string is synthesized live with a Karplus-Strong model instead of samples, so the whole thing is about 72 KB and works offline.

projects.name: Keyboard Tutor
projects.description: Play the keys, build chords, train your ear, keep time. Works with the computer keyboard or a MIDI controller, generates its own sound, and needs no account or backend.

projects.name: LiveBlock
projects.description: An ad blocker that works at the display layer instead of inside the browser, so it covers apps and streams too. Detection runs on device.

profile.intro: Hi! I'm Adam and I love technology and making things. This site has a little bit about me — you can find more on [webworldwide.online](https://webworldwide.online/).
profile.secondary: In my free time I collect CDs and vinyl. I'm trying to learn the guitar and make beats. I just love pursuing whatever creative endeavor comes to mind.

bullets: Backend engineer on HealthCare.gov (the CMS Federally Facilitated Marketplace): eligibility, enrollment and notice services.
Fixed eligibility logic that gave still-enrolled Medicaid/CHIP members the wrong decision, and raised its test coverage from 96.7% to 100%.
Converted and repaired 144 legacy API docs into 163 OpenAPI 3.0 specs for the new API gateway, and ran the team's training on it.

projects.name: Ultron
projects.what: Self-verifying AI coding harness; a drop-in replacement for Claude Code.
bullets: Developed it as one self-contained program (12,000+ tests) that won't report work done until the tests pass.
Outscored Claude Code on a 50-task SWE-bench Pro sample (37 vs. 35 solved) and ran at 0.77× its cost over 274 further tasks.
Secured it with a sandbox for Linux, macOS and Windows that IT can lock down, plus a tamper-evident audit log.
Trained a 2.4 MB built-in model that picks the right tool among 5,279 skills in 0.6 ms with 92% precision, fully offline.

projects.name: Vision
projects.what: Control center for running many AI coding agents at once.
bullets: Built a desktop app that runs many agents across projects, each on its own isolated copy of the code.
Designed it to mark work "Verified" only when the build and tests pass, and to share one real Chrome browser with the user.
Solo-built apps and a blog on a self-hosted CMS (Docker, Caddy, Cloudflare Tunnel).

projects.name: FileID
bullets: Shipped an app that sorts entire photo and document libraries offline, using on-device AI models for images, text and faces.
Added chat that answers questions about the library with citations, combining keyword and embedding search with a local LLM.
Developed native macOS, Windows and Linux apps (4,000+ tests, no telemetry), now converging on one shared Rust core.

projects.name: Media Shuttle
projects.what: Copies camera memory cards and blocks erasing until every copy is checksum-verified.
bullets: Hashes every file with SHA-256 on the card and at the destination, and keeps a copy only when the two match.
Unlocks erase only after a verified transfer, re-checks every file against its copy first, and refuses if anything is unverified.
Ships for macOS (signed and notarized, with Apple Photos import and a menu bar panel), Windows and Linux.

projects.name: Document Finder
projects.what: Searches eight open-access sources and serves chunked, cited results to AI tools over MCP.
bullets: Queries arXiv, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Europe PMC, Internet Archive, DOAJ, Zenodo and Project Gutenberg at once, plus a built-in web meta-search.

projects.name: Anchor
projects.what: Browser extension that keeps a paused video paused until you press play.

bullets: Kept the county's emergency radio (P25), microwave and computer networks running at 99.9% uptime.
Diagnosed and resolved technical issues using network analyzers and RF tools; performed system upgrades and preventative maintenance.
Worked with contractors and first responders to deploy secure, reliable communication infrastructure that met operational and regulatory standards.
Developed a Location Panel using TypeScript and Angular for the J.B. Hunt shipment platform, providing map coordinates and user submitted comments.
Team Lead for the Design System Interns Team, participating in daily standups to present our work.
Worked with various custom J.B. Hunt Angular components based on PrimeNG components.
Wrote new Storybook stories for J.B. Hunt components to meet CSF3 (Component Story Format 3) standards, written in TypeScript.
Led nine student groups and secured $18,000+ from student council for AI servers.
Developed and managed many new ACM services and events, including MegaMiner AI (revived), a new ACM Wiki, an online storefront for ACM merchandise, an ACM file server and the ACM general website.
Created a new ACM Logistics Officer position to help with the organization and functionality of ACM.

Worked with the Treasurer, Vice-President Internal, Vice-President External and Logistics Officer to organize events, manage conflicts, provide resources, and work with Administration for ACM and all its SIGs.
Cultivated partnerships with six corporate sponsors, securing financial backing and organizing the professional networking events around them.
Ran event logistics and scheduling as the primary liaison between the chapter and corporate representatives.
Minor in Mathematics. Dean's List twice.
Undergraduate research assistant in Computer Science (2024); web support for the mst.edu sites (2022–2024).

cards.title: Hey! 👋
body: Thanks for taking the time to check out my website and learn a little about me. So first let me introduce myself. My name is Adam Nolle. I am a graduate of Missouri University of Science and Technology (or Missouri S&T). I have a B.S. in Computer Science and Computer Engineering with a Minor in Mathematics. From January 2023 to May I was the President of my school's ACM (Association for Computing Machinery) chapter. In my time as President, I brought back our annual MegaMiner event, helped to renovate the second floor CS lounge in our school's Computer Science building, and more!
I currently work at Accenture Federal Services (AFS) full time!

cards.title: (Content) Creator 🎨
body: I love creating things, including digital "content" online for people to enjoy and learn from. I put most of my creative time into my YouTube channel and blog (both named Web World Wide) which are linked in the nav bar above! I love talking about things on my mind.

cards.title: Tech Nerd 🤓
body: If it's technology, I am interested. I have a "Homelab", a 3D Printer, and have built 6 computers (so far, and no, not just for me). This hobby continues to grow for me which is all I can ask for.

cards.title: Music Enjoyer 🎶
body: I enjoy music as most people do 😅. Recently I have started collecting vinyl and CDs of some of my favorite albums (💸). I think supporting artists and owning your media is really important. Also, have you been to a local record store? It's a ton of fun!
I also enjoy making beats in FL Studio and Logic, a hobby I picked up over the summer of 2023. I haven't started posting them yet, but if I do, I will be sure to link them here!
